Motherhood regret: why is it so taboo?

I read most the article and it seems like the common complaint was, "kids are hard and require all of my attention". What baffles me is where the idea that having kids was a part-time job. Being a parent, either parent, is a full time thing. And it shouldn't be up to the government to fix things, parents need to step up and help each other.

As a father, I work harder than I ever did before to support them. I didn't put in extra hours, spent my own money on additional training, and take risks because it seemed like fun thing to do. It was a boat load of stress, and I did it for my family. When I get home from work, I'm expected by my wife to help out. My kids expect me to give them attention.

Being a parent is hard, when it gets to be too much my wife goes out of her way to ensure I have a guys night. Similarly, when things are tough for her I make sure to give her a night out. I also arrange one date with her each month.

Growing up I remember the kids with the happiest parents were the ones who have their kids every minute of the day but without fail had a date night every Friday. The answer isn't more government intervention, it's parents being rational and realizing that sure, you can have those feelings but you never let your kids even think you feel that way. Make a little time for yourself and your spouse, no one can do that but you.
